svg.aria-label: Windows: Radeon RX 7000 and RX 6000 at 1440p: how much less time FSR 4 takes per frame with this project's builds than with AMD's own, moving scene, Balanced. Radeon RX 7900 XTX (1440p, 1 report): exact 28%, lossy 48%, less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 12%, 4.1.2l-lossy no report less than AMD's Lite. Radeon RX 7900 XT (1440p, 2 reports): exact 21%, lossy 43%, less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 12%, 4.1.2l-lossy 17% less than AMD's Lite. Radeon RX 7700 XT (1440p, 6 reports): exact 33%, lossy 51%, less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 2%, 4.1.2l-lossy 14% less than AMD's Lite. Radeon RX 7600 (1440p, 8 reports): exact 25%, lossy 42%, less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 16%, 4.1.2l-lossy 21% less than AMD's Lite. Radeon RX 6800 XT (1440p, 4 reports): exact 4%, lossy 25%, less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 12%, 4.1.2l-lossy 15% less than AMD's Lite. Radeon RX 6800 (1440p, 6 reports): exact 2%, lossy 25%, less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 13%, 4.1.2l-lossy 16% less than AMD's Lite. Radeon RX 6750 XT (1440p, 14 reports): exact 2%, lossy 24%, less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 11%, 4.1.2l-lossy 14% less than AMD's Lite. Radeon RX 6700 XT (1440p, 1 report): exact 2%, lossy 24%, less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 12%, 4.1.2l-lossy 14% less than AMD's Lite. Radeon RX 6650 XT (1440p, 2 reports): exact 4%, lossy 23%, less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 8%, 4.1.2l-lossy 12% less than AMD's Lite. Radeon RX 6600 XT (1440p, 1 report): exact 6%, lossy no report, less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 8%, 4.1.2l-lossy no report less than AMD's Lite. Radeon RX 6600 (1440p, 2 reports): exact 3%, lossy 23%, less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 9%, 4.1.2l-lossy 14% less than AMD's Lite.
svg.text: Windows: Radeon RX 7000 and RX 6000 at 1440p
How much less time FSR 4 takes per frame than with AMD's own. Longer is faster.
Testers' timing-kit reports (test packs 2026-11-18 to 2026-11-20), each build against AMD's in the same report, median per card. 1080p and 4K: the table below.
The two panels have different scales: 0 to 60% on the left, 0 to 25% on the right.
